title: Wire brushes, hi-hat and low boy pedals
summary: Frazier talks about wire brushes and his first hi-hat in the late 1930s.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Early drum kits and the gear drummers used

blocks.x: and then you can take your wire brushes on your drum and don't drown them man I'd play soft you know take two sticks of wire brushes when that phrase come on this beat nice and soft and don't drown them out. When did wire brushes come in? Yeah they come in but they've been here wire brushes some drummers used to adopt them with one stick and one wire. I still do that to the day. Alfred does that too. Yeah one stick you can tell all the old jazz drummers but a real these fellas in the latest late 30s they'll take two wire brushes and they play everything right there they won't use a drum stick. Like in the dog swimming. Yeah they just keep that all the way through. They won't use a stick. What about a hi-hat or sock symbol did you ever try those? Yeah. Or use them much?
